name: Wisconsin
overview: Wisconsin combines refundable homestead relief, a nonrefundable income-tax property/rent credit, veteran refunds and several separate property-bill credits.

programs.name: Homestead Credit
programs.ageRule: 18 or older; positive earned income, disability, or claimant/spouse age 62 or older also required.
programs.incomeDefinition: Broad taxable/nontaxable household income, loss/depreciation adjustments and $500 qualifying-dependent deduction.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-adjusted credit based on allowable assessed property taxes or rent constituting property taxes; rent share depends on heat inclusion.
programs.application: File Schedule H or H-EZ with tax bill/rent certificate; most 2025 claims due April 15, 2030.
eligibilityNotes: Public assistance and tax-exempt housing can affect allowance.
interactions: Cannot claim with veterans/surviving-spouses property-tax credit on same 2025 taxes or farmland preservation credit.

programs.name: School Property Tax Credit
programs.formulaSummary: Income-tax credit based on eligible property taxes or rent; owner and renter amounts are combined subject to one cap, with rent table depending on heat inclusion.
eligibilityNotes: Uses taxes paid in 2025, unlike Homestead's assessed-tax basis.

programs.name: Veterans and Surviving Spouses Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: WDVA-certified eligible veteran or unremarried surviving spouse.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible property taxes paid on principal dwelling and up to one acre.
programs.formulaSummary: Refunds qualifying paid property taxes; excludes special assessments, interest, service charges and business-use taxes.
programs.application: Obtain WDVA certification and claim through income-tax return.
interactions: Cannot combine on same taxes with Homestead credit.

sources.title: Veterans and surviving spouses property-tax credit

programs.name: Lottery and Gaming Credit
programs.maximumBenefit: Applicable school rate times credit value up to $27,000 for 2025/26.
programs.formulaSummary: Bill-level credit based on the smaller of qualifying property value and state maximum credit value.
programs.application: File application with county or eligible municipal treasurer.
eligibilityNotes: Wisconsin resident owner using property as primary residence on January 1, 2025.

sources.title: 2025–26 Lottery and First Dollar maximum credit values

programs.name: First Dollar Credit
programs.maximumBenefit: Local calculated credit based on maximum credit value of $9,000 in 2025/26.
programs.formulaSummary: Automatic property-bill credit on qualifying improved parcels, varying by school tax rate.

sources.title: 2025–26 Lottery and First Dollar maximum credit values

programs.name: School Levy Tax Credit
programs.formulaSummary: State payments to counties and municipalities reduce property-tax bills; allocation depends on school levies.
programs.application: Applied through local property-tax billing, not income-tax return.
eligibilityNotes: Property-owner relief can cover rental property; it is not a direct renter payment.

researchNotes: Lottery/Gaming, First Dollar, and School Levy credits normally already reduce net property-tax bills; do not add them again to an input already measured after bill credits.
School Property Tax Credit and School Levy Tax Credit are different programs.
Veteran eligibility requires WDVA certification; this inventory does not infer eligibility from a single disability-percentage input.
